Every place had its certain unwritten rules. A rite of passage, if you will, to be considered one of the people, to feel as if they truly belonged somewhere.

The Styxian custom of gathering flowers from one of the three big gardens that belonged to the youngest princess and later weaving the most fragrant flowers into crowns was something that usually came to mind when one thought of the ancient kingdom. Janusopolis, on another hand, was known for attracting curious people from all over the world, trying to understand the mysteries of the universe and the intricacies of destiny that were woven into stars. Only to later find a prophecy that was shoved into the depths of the dusty library – half forgotten, half hidden – and learn that all their findings meant nothing and, in fact, had been foretold a millennia ago.

A small village like Aedes Elysiae had no such elaborate unwritten rules – the people there were friendly and all it took for them to consider someone a friend was a simple participation in the welcoming feast and some help in the golden fields. As long as one completed those tasks, they were already considered a dear friend of everyone.

Phainon has traveled all over Amphoreus and when she first stepped foot into Castrum Kremnos she assumed, just like any normal person, that it too had its rules. She tried to find out what exactly they were but for the first time in her life, no one could give her a proper answer. Even okhemans, who were widely known for their capricious natures and love to debate everything under the sun, were not as secretive about their rules as seemingly open and straightforward kremnoans.

(Though Phainon wasn’t sure if getting caught in one of Okhema’s Goldweaver threads could even be considered a ‘rite of passage.’ Phainon has done it so often in the time she was in Okhema that she must be considered a dear family to Lady Aglaea at this point.)

But Kremnos remained a mystery to Phainon. Even when she decided to stay for a longer time, no longer moving from one kingdom to another in search for who-knew-what that was hidden who-knew-where; even when she strolled down the streets, her head swirling from one colorful display of antiques to another, trying to take everything all at once; even when she made dozens of friends after visiting different little food stalls to better familiarize herself not only with the locals but also with the food they had – it was still a mystery.

It was only when Phainon, fresh out of training that somehow ended with her getting a job as one of the outer guards of the palace – that she had finally out the truth.

They were celebrating her upcoming promotion – Phainon didn’t even know how she ended up being one of the guards that were chosen for the upcoming birthday celebration of the Crown Princess but she wasn’t complaining. A job was a job and she didn’t mind being a guard for a while.

“Hey,” one of the guards waved his pint of wine in her face. Phainon batted his hand away with a laugh. “You’ve been all over Amphoreus, weren’t you? Tells us,” he asked conspiratorially, “is that true that the Queen of Styxia can turn into a dragon?”

They were already halfway drunk, everything seemed funny and this just sent Phainon over the edge. She laughed, clutching the side of table. “No,” she rasped. “Not true!”

A chorus of groans was heard across the table.

“But!” she raised her finger. She lowered her voice, “They do have a dragon. An absolutely gorgeous girl. So friendly!”

“You petted a dragon?”

“Yep!” Phainon said with a pop and then with a wave of her hand, “I even put a flower crown on her. T’is one of Styxia’s unwritten rules.”

“Unwritten rules?”

Phainon nodded. She wasn’t fully drunk but she could feel it getting to her. She pushed another pint of wine away with a shake of her head. “I’m good,” and then continued, “Yeah, y’know. ‘Unwritten rules’. A rite of passage. A thing everyone has to try or do at least once when they’re visiting a new place.”

An inner palace guard, Penelope, twirled a dark lock around her finger. “Like getting tangled in Lady Goldweaver’s golden threads when you’re in Okhema?”

“Or,” another added, “like jumping off a cliff in Bulsa!”

Phainon hummed. “Yeah, something like that.” And then she asked, curious. “Do you have that here?”

There was a beat of silence as everyone seemed to think about it. Then one of the guards snorted.

“Something like that.”

“Oh?”

The guard took a sip of his wine. “The Crown Princess.”

Suddenly everyone averted their eyes. Phainon, clueless to what was going on, cocked her head to the side. “What about her?”

“Have you seen her?”

Phainon shook her head. “Not yet, no.”

A girl sitting opposite of her blushed a deep, deep red. She hid her face in her hands.

“You’ll know when you see her then,” someone in the back said, their gaze faraway. “The Crown Princess. That’s the true rite of passage in Castrum Kremnos.”

“The line is secured. Everything should be in order. Proceed with the preparations.”

The Crown Princess’ birthday was right around the corner and, as it always was during that time, the celebration that was thrown in her honor would stretch for days. It was a big event that usually involved a lot of dignitaries from all corners of Amphoreus visiting to pay respects and, as Phainon has learned recently, in hopes to catch a glimpse of the elusive Crown Princess.

Even Phainon, who at that point had worked as a guard for a few months, had yet to see her face to face. She had only caught a glimpse of the princess once, but even then she had only managed to see a tall silhouette of a woman with a head full of strawberry blond curls that cascaded down a smooth expanse of her back. By the time Phainon realized just who it was, the princess was ushered to another room by her horde of personal guards.

She was said to be a beauty, one that ensnared people in her grasp with a mere glance. Rumored to look like her mother – the Queen – Princess Mydei was a beloved daughter of Castrum Kremnos, a worthy heir that would one day become its Queen.

Phainon wasn’t sure about princess’ beauty – but if she actually took after her mother than her good looks were all but guaranteed because Phainon had the chance to meet Queen Gorgo before and all she could think at the moment was that King Eurypon was one lucky bastard.

Thought all in her head, of course. She had no desire to be accused of treason for insulting the king.

But the last part? ‘Beloved daughter of Castrum Kremnos’? That was all true. Not a day has passed that Phainon hasn’t heard at least one person singing praises to their beloved princess. She was adored by the people but Phainon wasn’t yet sure if it was a devotion most people seemed to harbor for their rulers, good or bad, or was this love born of genuine feelings and appreciation.

But it wasn’t her job to speculate and frankly Phainon didn’t care.

Not like she’d ever cross paths with the princess anyway.

“Hey,” another bodyguard, Andreas, suddenly elbowed Phainon when she was about to put on her helmet. “Your position will be by the princess. Guarding her will be your main duty until the celebration ends.”

Speak of the devil and she shall appear.

Phainon furrowed her brows. “What? But the back venue –”

“Change of plans. I would’ve done It myself but,” he waved his hand at the doors, “can’t move from my own post. You’ll have to do. Don’t worry, you won’t be the only one – the princess’ personal guards will be there with you.”

“That’s… Fine. Why me though?”

“Well,” Andreas looked her up and down. “You’re the strongest guard we have and you’re a woman. The princess might feel more comfortable with you.”

Phainon raised her eyebrow skeptically. She pointed at her helmet, “Fine but I don’t think it matters much, not when I have this thing on.”

The armor the outer guards wore was all in dark colors. Fully covered and with a cape so long not an inch of skin could be spied, much less the contours of Phainon’s body. Her being a woman didn’t even matter not when her face was all covered up and the bulky armor made her half a head taller – and that was considering that Phainon towered over most people on her regular days in general. With the armor on she was practically gigantic. Even Andreas that was not a small man by any means had to tilt his head up to meet her eyes.

“Whatever,” she slicked her short hair down and plopped the helmet on. She turned around with a small wave of her gloved hand. “The princess will be safe in my hands, don’t worry.”

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

“You must be the outer guard,” one of the princess’ personal guards remarked. Clad in a signature blue light armor, he smiled at Phainon that was positioned at the back, dark shadows covering her body. “I’m Hephaestion, the main personal guard of the Crown Princess.”

Phainon nodded, not moving from her place. “Phainon,” came her distorted voice.

Hephaestion smiled, quickly introducing her to other guards that were peering at her curiously from behind Hephaestion’s back. “So,” he said once he was done. “I assume they haven’t told you why you were transferred here?”

Phainon frowned. “Were they supposed to?”

She assumed it was a simple change of plans because some of the guards got sick or something. No big deal, it wasn’t like getting suddenly transferred to guard the princess changed much in her schedule. A job was a job.

Peucesta and Hephaestion shared a look.

“It’d make explaining everything easier, that’s for sure…” Peucesta started. “Have you seen the new additions to the guest list?”

“Yes. Some distant family member of the Tretos royalty?”

The guards nodded. “Yes. Him.”

Phainon raised her eyebrows, still not understanding the correlation. “And what is wrong with him?”

“He…” Peucesta started but then fell silent, looking awkwardly at his friends.

“He is one of many suitors of the Crown Princess,” Leonnius suddenly said. He propped his chin on hand as he leaned in his chair. He frowned. “Except that he is one of the… Insistent ones. The princess has rejected him many times and yet he refuses to give up.”

Phainon cocked her head to the side. “Why is he still allowed in the palace then?”

“Kremnos doesn’t want to severe our trade relationship with Tretos. The King wanted to ban him anyway, trade relationship be damned, but the princess asked to let her handle it on her own,” Leonnius shrugged.

“The King allowed it but decided to tighten the security. Just in case,” Hephaestion added, looking at Phainon.

“And that’s why I’m here.”

“And that’s why you’re here,” Hephaestion repeated. He rubbed his forehead with a small wince. “Sir Krateros told the King that you are the strongest outer guard we currently have,” he peered at Phainon’s bulky armor and the heavy greatsword she carried on her back. “I assume he was right in that assessment.”

She shrugged, not refuting the compliment. She was the strongest – it was a simple fact. There was no need to play coy.

“I have my ways,” Phainon said. She pushed off the wall she was leaning on and strode next to the guards, finally stepping into the sun. Heavy boots clunked as she stood right behind the other guards, like a dark shadow towering over all of them. She rolled her shoulders. “Okay. When do we start?”

Protect the princess from her insistent suitor, Phainon thought as she followed Hephaestion through the back door that would lead them directly to the Crown Princess’ chambers. Easy enough.

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

Okay, she thought a little dazed when she first saw the Crown Princess as she conversed with her parents in front of her chambers. Phainon swallowed hard, praying that nobody noticed her little stumble. Can’t blame the King for being overly cautious.

The Princess was a vison in her long-sleeved teal dress with the silk fabric hugging every dip and every curve of her hourglass figure – it highlighted the subtle strength of her shoulders, the inward sweep of her waist and the wide flare of her hips. Her golden curls were swept into an elaborate updo, baring the tan expanse of her back to the world, every shift of muscle and stark line of her spine on full display.

Hearing the commotion, the Crown Princess turned around, her parents and their guards following shortly.

Phainon drew a sharp breath. The rumors didn’t do her justice.

Princess Mydei did take after her mother. And standing beside Queen Gorgo, the resemblance was unmistakable – the same bone structure, the same proud bearing. But where Queen Gorgo was slightly softer, the planes of her face mellowed out with age, Princess Mydei was all brash strokes and sharp angles that had not lost its inherit elegance. She was full of contradictions – half-lidded eyes that keenly followed each guard’s move, a soft mouth that pursed thoughtfully as her gaze landed on Phainon. Even her hair defied containment: a wild mane of strawberry-blond curls barely restrained by the golden pins, as if her very essence refused to be tamed.

Princess Mydei took a step forward, her eyes not leaving Phainon’s frame. Phainon felt the weight of that stare like a physical thing, pressing against her armor. “You must be the guard my father had chosen for today’s celebration.”

Her voice matched her face – low and controlled, with a certain edge that suggested she was accustomed to being answered promptly and truthfully.

Phainon lowered her head. A bead of sweat slowly rolled down her neck. “Yes, Your Highness,” she replied, for the first time ever thanking every Titan – alive or dead – that her helmet concealed her face and disguised her true voice. 

The Princess let out a soft contemplative hum when she noticed the greatsword attached to Phainon’s back. The weapon was nearly as tall as she was, its worn leather grip speaking of years of use. Something flickered across the princess’ face. She gave a short sharp nod, “You’ll do.”

Phainon let out a shaky breath as she straightened out.

Princess Mydei turned to her parents. “Mother, father. I will see you at the celebration.”

And without another word she strode away, her steps quick and purposeful, leaving her guards to scramble in her wake.

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

“I understand my father is worried,” Princess Mydei said, not bothering to look back as they made their way to the celebration hall. “But should anything happen, none of you will need to intervene.” 

She turned her head slightly, casting a look over her shoulder. The other guards immediately lowered their gazes, silent. Phainon, however, kept her eyes fixed on the Princess.

They reached the grand ornamental doors. As Ptolemy and Perdikkas each took a handle to pull them open for her, the Princess stopped. She turned and looked directly at Phainon.

“I can handle matters on my own,” she stated, holding Phainon's gaze through the helmet's eye-slit, waiting for a sign of acknowledgment. The words were meant for all of them, but her eyes never left Phainon's helmet. 

Phainon didn’t lower her head. She met the Princess's stare, invisible behind her helmet. “Whatever you say, princess.”

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

Huh, Phainon watched the ‘suitor’ wilt under the ice-cold glare of the princess. Maybe she was right.

The princess sat in her place, receiving guests with practiced grace. One priceless gift after another, each welcomed with a small smile and a warm – or what Phainon assumed was considered to be warm for the princess – welcome. That is, until the royals from Tretos approached. The shift in her demeanor was instantaneous.

Phainon's hand tightened on her greatsword though she held her position. Her focus narrowed to the Princess and the young man that was now vying so desperately for her attention.

The Princess noticed a movement from the corner of her eye and shot her a silent look. Phainon’s gloves creaked as she gripped her weapon. She didn’t move.

A minute passed. Phainon couldn’t hear what they were talking about, she was too far away for it, but the sudden change in Hephaestion’s expression and the princess’ spine turning rigid told her all she needed to know. The conversation must have turned deeply unpleasant for everyone involved.

The man from Tretos raised his head, looking hopelessly at the princess but she remained unmoved. Then her voice rang out, clear and commanding. “Guards. This man is feeling unwell. Please escort him to his rooms.”

The man started to protest, but before anyone could move Phainon was already at his side. Her grip on his shoulders was firm, brooking no argument. She looked towards the princess and inclined her head in a formal bow.  “Of course, Your Highness.”

Princess Mydei’s painted red lips curved into a small smile.

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

The celebration continued without a hitch.

A week later, Phainon was halfway through her morning drills when a messenger from the Head of the Guard arrived with a single, curt order: gather her belongings and vacate the outer guard's dormitory by sundown.

That same evening, in a brief ceremony devoid of fanfare, the King himself promoted her to the ranks of the inner palace guard.

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

“Hope you missed working with us,” Perdikkas joked as he strapped more potions to his belt.

It’s been a few months since Phainon was promoted. Being an inner palace guard had many perks – better food, better training grounds, better weapons. Hell, even better accommodations. Phainon loved her colleagues in the outer guard but she didn’t miss the outer guard's dormitory that constantly smelled like sweat, cheap oil and twenty unwashed men.

She wouldn’t give up the little room that came with her new rank for anything in the world.

Phainon snorted, the sound coming out much raspier thanks to her helmet. She tightened the straps that held her greatsword before she replied. “As if. We work together every other week; what’s there to miss?”

The anniversary of the King and Queen’s thirty years of marriage was about to begin and once more the king had ordered Phainon to stay by his daughter’s side.

Ever since her promotion, she worked closely with the Crown Princess and her personal guards. She quickly familiarized herself with her new duties – that weren’t really all that different from what she used to do before – and so far she was doing great. Amazing even.

If it only wasn’t for…

“The princess is almost done. Let’s go.”

Her.

Phainon was a professional. She had always been able to easily separate her work from the messy and complicated personal feelings. In all years she was working, through postings that had placed her in close proximity to charming nobles and striking knights, she had never once lost her footing.

Phainon rolled her shoulders as she followed Perdikkas. Her steps were strong and measured against the marble floor of the palace.

Until the Crown Princess.

Phainon pressed her lips into a thin line behind her helmet. 

“You’ll know when you see her then. The Crown Princess. That’s the true rite of passage in Castrum Kremnos.”

Well, consider her convinced. She now knew why everyone in Kremnos was so taken with their princess.

She had heard the stories, of course. From many people, be it outer, inner guards or simple civilians on the streets, who had never held a sword but still spoke of the princess with a particular softness in their eyes. 

“It was a simple youthful infatuation,” a baker on the street near Phainon’s old apartment once told her. She handed her a warm pastry with a knowing smile. “You get over it eventually.”

Phainon remembered listening to these stories with polite interest. She was curious, yes, but she knew that would have to be one of those customs that would never affect her. Not only because at that time she wasn’t planning on staying in Castrum Kremnos for long but more so because she was confident in her immunity. She was calm, level headed especially when matters of the heart were involved.

There would be no crushes, no infatuations. Nothing.

The Crown Princess has existed on an entirely different plane of society and Phainon wasn’t one to entertain such thoughts.

That’s what she thought, at least, before she became an outer guard. Then an inner guard.

Before she had to come face to face with the princess on multiple occasions and watch her deal with each matter swiftly and efficiently, as if she was born to do just that. Before she was forced to take a closer look and realize there was more behind that pretty face than she originally thought.

And suddenly such thoughts stopped sounding as silly as they did in the past. Suddenly, she understood why the baker had smiled that knowing smile. Why the old soldiers told their stories with a fond exasperation rather than embarrassment. 

Everyone treated it like a fond memory. Something so common that they had long stopped paying attention to it.

And now, Phainon was no different.

The doors leading to Princess Mydei's chambers loomed ahead, ornate and massive.

Phainon gripped her greatsword.

It was time to face the music.

-ˋˏ ༻❁✿❀༺ ˎˊ-

The celebration of the King and Queen's anniversary was going beautifully.

The great hall was bright with light and color. The crystal chandelier caught the glow of a thousand candles and scattered rainbow fragments across the marble walls. Musicians played from a gallery overhead, their melodies weaving through the happy murmur of nobles and visiting dignitaries. The happy couple sat on their thrones, their hands intertwined and faces glowing. They looked for all the world like two people who had forgotten, just for this one evening, the weight of their crowns.

Phainon stood at her post near the eastern wall, close enough to the high table to observe but far enough to remain unobtrusive. Her gaze swept across the room in practiced intervals – the guests, the exits, the other guards, the guests again. Princess Mydei sat to her mother's right, resplendent in a deep crimson dress that made her strawberry-blond curls blaze like captured fire. She was laughing at something her father had said, head tilted back, her throat a long, elegant line.

Stop looking, Phainon told herself firmly. Professional. You're a professional.

She looked away. Counted the exits. Counted the guests. Without her knowledge her gaze locked on the laughing Crown Princess once more.

Thank God for the helmet, Phainon thought as she watched the princess brush her hair away from her face with practiced elegance.

Phainon slumped a little, leaning harder against the wall. The celebration was going great.

Until it wasn’t.

The first hint that something was wrong was the smell.

Smoke.

Phainon’s head snapped to the service corridor. The doors to the kitchen were closed – they were always closed during formal events, to keep the noise and chaos of food preparation separate from the celebration hall – but a thin wisp of grey was beginning to curl beneath the doors.

Phainon took a step forward, her hand finding the grip of her greatsword. Around the room other guards were beginning to notice too, their postures shifting from relaxed vigilance to something sharper.

Then the screaming started.

First from the kitchen, then quickly spreading to the guests. The musicians stumbled to a halt, their instruments clattering against the gallery rail.

And then, with a roar that shook the very stones of the palace, the fire announced itself.

The kitchen doors exploded outward.

Flame rushed through the opening like a living thing, hungry and eager. It licked at tapestries with terrifying speed, making the guests scramble as they surged away from the heat, all manners forgotten in the face of primal need of survival.

“Phainon!” the voice cut through the chaos like a blade. Phainon’s head snapped up. “Take the princess and run!” Hephaestion yelled as he ducked under a table when a chandelier swayed overhead, its crystals chiming dangerously.

“We’ll take care of everything else. Just take the princess away!”

As soon as he finished talking, the chandelier finally crashed to the floor, sending up a spray of flame and shattered crystals in all directions. Hephaestion yelped and dove back under the nearest table, disappearing from view.

Phainon was already moving.

Her head snapped towards the princess, eyes finding her immediately. Princess Mydei was already on her feet, her brows furrowed as she was gripping her mother’s hand. She quickly handed her mother to her father, not even a second wasted as she directed them to their guards. But despite seeming so calm in the face of the fire, Phainon could see the tension in every line of her body, the way her chest moved a little too quickly beneath the crimson silk.

“Your Highness!” Phainon was at her side a second later, her voice barely audible above the roar of the flames. “We need to move. Now!”

The princess snapped her head to Phainon, a protest ready on her lips and her gold eyes glinting with dangerous light. But before she could even utter a word, King Eurypon stepped from behind Queen Gorgo and with a strong hand shoved his daughter in Phainon’s hands.

Not expecting it, Princess Mydei stumbled. Phainon quickly helped her right herself, pressing her close to her dark armor and shielding her from the heat of the flames.

“Father!”

“We need to stay here and ensure everyone’s safety but you need to go!” the king shouted to his daughter. And then he turned to Phainon, “Take her! Keep her safe!” 

Without another word, Phainon grabbed Princess Mydei’s hand and pulled her to the exit. Mydei stumbled once more, the hem of her long dress catching on her heels. She caught herself and then they were running, side by side, away from the spreading flames and toward the nearest exit.

Behind them, Phainon heard the King's voice roaring orders and the Queen's directing guards and guests alike. She shook her head and focused on the hand that was gripping hers as they run to the exit.

After another stumble, Phainon threw away all decency and decorum that was beaten into her in all these months spent as the guard of the palace. With fire licking at their heels, she grabbed the princess by the waist and, with another surge of power, she threw her over her shoulder. Princess Mydei yelped, a completely undignified sound that Phainon would have treasured under any other circumstances, and then she was upside down, draped over Phainon's shoulder like a sack of particularly furious grain.

Ignoring the princess’ screams and punches that were reverberating through her armor – Titans help her, the woman was strong – she broke free from the hall. Without even looking and with the princess firmly in her grasp Phainon ran towards the closest palace’s exit.

“Just because my father ordered you to save me, doesn’t mean that you get to toss me around like a sack of potatoes!” Princess Mydei tried to slip away from Phainon’s grasp, her voice full of righteous fury. “Now let go of me, you brute!”

Phainon ignored her protests, her hand tightening on the princess thighs. Another punch revibrated through her armor. Phainon cringed, her head ringing from the constant onslaught.

Fucking hell.

“Your Highness, please. Just wait until I get us out of the palace,” she tried to bargain, her voice strained between the breaths. She only got a kick to her chest for that.

“Let go of me. Now.”

Phainon sighed and ran faster. There were out of the immediate danger zone but it was still uncomfortably warm – they only just managed to escape the fire. It wasn’t safe yet.

Her legs burned under the weight of the heavy armor but she didn’t stop running.

Another kick. This time to her chest which meant the princess somehow managed to change positions even with Phainon’s firm grip on her.

Phainon staggered slightly but quickly recovered, her hand tightening on those thighs in a grip that was toeing the line of professional but was definitely necessary with how the slippery princess kept trying to escape from Phainon, making her hands slip up towards her bottom each time she moved.

“Your Highness… Please do not dent my chestplate.”

“Then,” another kick, which definitely did dent the chestplate. “Let go of me!”

Phainon felt the metal give way, pressing inward against her ribs, and made a mental note to request reimbursement from the royal treasury.

She sighed, the sound lost inside her helmet.

Phainon didn’t slow down, not until they were through the outer doors and the night air hit their faces, cooling them down almost instantly. Only once Phainon was sure they were a safe distance away from any possible collapse or secondary fire, did she stop and carefully lowered the wildcat pretending to be a princess to the ground.

The princess landed on her feet with unexpected grace. Her hair had escaped its elaborate styling, blond curls exploding in every direction. Her crimson dress was rumpled, smudged with soot and slightly torn at one shoulder, as she glared at Phainon with enough fury to set Phainon and probably the whole palace on fire all over again.
